City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Financing Authority, Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*
September 17, 2012
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 05:04 p.m. , on September 17, 2012, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on September 12, 2012, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
Present:
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Leckness
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Ury
Absent:
Council Member Schlicht
Staff Present:
Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
William P. Curley III, City Attorney
Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
INVOCATION: Council Member Leckness
CLOSED SESSION
CS1.
Labor Negotiation's - The City Council will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations are the City and the City's Unrepresented Employees. The City's Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.
RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE
At the hour of 5:06 p.m,. Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened at 6:04 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member Schlicht was absent.)
REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION
City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council received an update and had a discussion on employee benefits. No conclusion was reached and there was no reportable action from Closed Session.
PRESENTATIONS
P1.
Presentation on the United States Constitution
The City Council and audience received a presentation from Benjamin Franklin (Historian Bob Hayes.)
P2.
Recognition of the South Mission Viejo Little League Championship Teams
Mayor Ury presented certificates of commendation to the coaches and members of the South Mission Viejo Little League championship teams.
P3.
Recognize the Mission Viejo Pony 8U All Star Pinto Division World Series Champions
Mayor Ury presented certificates of commendation to the coaches and members of the Pony 8U All Star Pinto Division World Series championship team.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Bill Moynihan, M.V.: thanked the City for hosting the WWII Veterans recognition luncheon at the Murray Center and for continually supporting military personnel.Desi J. Kiss, M.V.: inquired about the City’s financial status and the amount of money in reserves. Mr. Kiss asked for a copy of the document Council Member Schlicht requested with regards to a secret San Onofre Nuclear power plant meeting and a copy of the City’s emergency and public evacuation plan.Dan Avery, M.V.: referring to a web site called stopthetackylights.com, he asked residents to be careful during an election year and to wade through the information they receive. Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: cautioned that there is the potential for rate increases for homes within the City’s Special Fire Protection Area. He stated that the City Attorney should seek confirmation from local real estate attorneys on the matter.
Kathleen Loewel, M.V.: thanked the Council Members for their service and asked for clarification on the budget and reserves.
CONSENT CALENDAR
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to approve the Consent Calendar as described below.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
Council Member Schlicht
1.
Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions
Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.
2.
City Council Minutes
Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of September 4, 2012, as presented.
3.
Check Register dated August 31, 2012 in the amount of $562,885.59
Ratified the accompanying check register.
4.
Microsoft Licensing Renewal
Approved the three-year agreement with Microsoft for Microsoft Product Licensing renewal and issue a purchase order to CompuCom for such services for 2012-13 in the amount of $62,960.52.
5.
City Treasurer's Monthly Report for July 2012
Received and filed.
6.
Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer's Monthly Report for July 2012
Received and filed.
7.
Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer's Monthly Report for July 2012
Received and filed.
8.
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer's Monthly Report for July 2012
Received and filed.
9.
Community Development Financing Authority (CDFA) Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2011-12 and Annual Review of the CDFA Investment Policy
(1) Received and filed the accompanying Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2011-12; and (2) adopted Resolution 12-03 Approving the Authority’s Investment Policy for FY2012-13.
10.
City Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2011-12 and Annual Review of City’s Investment Policy
(1) Received and file the accompanying City Treasurer’s Annual Report for fiscal year 2011-12; (2) adopted Resolution 12-55 Approving the City’s Investment Policy for FY 2012-13; and (3) set the Benchmark Index for FY 2012-13 to be a Government Securities Index comprised of 60% three-month Treasury Bills; 25% Treasury and Agency securities with maturities greater than one year and up to three years; and 15% Treasury and Agency securities with maturities greater than three years and up to five years.
11.
Designation of Positions Authorized to Apply for Federal and State Financial Assistance
Adopted Resolution 12-56 Authorizing Certain Positions to Act as Agents for the Purpose of Obtaining Federal Financial Assistance and/or State Financial Assistance.
12.
Use of Supplemental Law Enforcement Services Fund
Approved the Use for the Supplemental Law Enforcement Services Fund.
13.
Orange County Transportation Authority 2012-2013 Comprehensive Transportation Funding Program Call-for-Projects
Adopted Resolution 12-57 Approving the Submittal of the Muirlands Boulevard Corridor, the Jeronimo Road Corridor, and the Trabuco Road Corridor Improvement Projects to the Orange County Transportation Authority for Funding Under the Competitive Measure M2 Regional Transportation Signal Synchronization Program (Project P).
PUBLIC HEARINGS
OLD BUSINESS
NEW BUSINESS
14.
2012 Speed Limit Update
Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report and answered the City Council Member’s questions.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to introduce Ordinance 12-295 Amending Chapter 12.04.010(d) of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code Regarding Prima Facie Speed Limits on Certain Streets, as amended.
Amendment: the speed limit for Pacific Hills Drive from Oso Parkway to South Ridge should have read 30 MPH and will be corrected for the Ordinance.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
Council Member Schlicht
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR
MAYOR'S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS
15.
Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report
Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: presented a letter to Council Member Kelley and asked for a response to his request for the status of a bid package for OCFA's broker/dealer work and whether or not OCFA has started an investigation into alleged fraudulent disability filings.
Council Member Kelley presented the report.
16.
Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Ury presented the report.
17.
San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon presented the report.
STAFF REPORTS
City Manager’s Report
18.
FY 2011/12 Budget Amendments and Carryovers and FY 2011/12 Budget Adjustments
City Manager Wilberg announced that at the close out of the 2011-12 fiscal year, there is a General Fund operating surplus of just under $1 million.
Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.
Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1) adopt Resolution 12-58 Amending the FY 2011/12 City Budget for Year-End Adjustments in Certain Accounts; and (2) adopt Resolution 12-59 Amending the FY 2012/13 City Budget to Reflect Final Carryovers from FY 2011/12 and Certain Other Adjustments.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
Council Member Schlicht
City Attorney’s Report
City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there are some new legal cases that may affect the City and he will follow up and provide additional information in the near future. Council Member Kelley stated that there have been reports from members of the public that conflict with the City Attorney’s opinion on the Special Fire Protection Area (SFPA) and she asked Mr. Curley to touch on the questions that have come up.
Mr. Curley responded that the disclosure requirements for real estate are expressly set in the California Civil Code and, by law, high fire hazard severity zone maps are required to be disclosed in real estate transactions. The City Council voted to reject those maps and instead established a Special Fire Protection Area which, by law, does not have to be disclosed.
Council Member Kelley encouraged residents to contact her with inquiries or visit the City’s web site for a fact sheet that will address many of the questions that continue to arise on the matter.
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS
19.
Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Kelley announced that she went to the California League of Cities conference last week. She got a lot of good information and found it beneficial to attend.
Council Member Leckness
20.
Smoke Alarm Program
Council Member Leckness presented his report.
Motion made by Council Member Leckness, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to direct staff to meet with OCFA representatives to pursue grants for a Smoke Alarm Program in Mission Viejo, including applying for funding through the United States Fire Administration Fire Prevention and Safety Grant Program.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
Council Member Schlicht
Council Member Leckness announced that earlier in the day he attended ribbon cutting ceremonies for the Navy Federal Credit Union and Apple Ranch Market and he spoke highly of these new businesses.
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon discussed her attendance at the recent League of California Cities conference and her membership on the League’s Administrative Services Committee. She noted that the committee has been evaluating Proposition 31 and has voted to not support it. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon encouraged residents to read through the measure before voting in November. She also outlined her attendance at the grand opening celebration of Apple Ranch Market and Navy Federal Credit Union. She encouraged residents to look into the credit union’s products and services as they have great deals and offer very good returns. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon thanked the Girl Scouts and Boy Scouts for the Patriot Day Ceremony and she thanked Samantha Trippe for the moving gesture to obtain a bio for all of the people killed on 9/11 and hand them out at the ceremony. She also discussed the upcoming screening of Behind the Orange Curtain , a film about accidental prescription drug overdoses. The movie will be shown on October 4, 2012, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. at the Murray Center. Also, on October 10, the Community of Character Committee will host an event for parents and teens to listen to a panel of medical experts, DEA representatives and people who have survived a prescription drug overdose. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that she attended the recent Explorers Program Spurgeon Awards luncheon and she asked, with the consent of her colleagues, to have staff submit a plan for renovating some of the city’s aging slopes and to provide a list of costs.
Mayor Ury
Mayor Ury stated that the Patriots Day ceremony was fantastic and he enjoyed being a part of it. He asked his colleagues for ideas for the million dollars that is being put back into reserves. He noted that he would like to put some programs in place that will impact the residents and he stated that this was an important meeting to attend for that reason. Mr. Ury asked the City Clerk to let him know when she heard that Council member Schlicht would not be at the meeting and to provide any supporting documentation for the record.
ADJOURNMENT
At the hour of 8:16 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, October 1, 2012, at 5:00 p.m.

Approved at the meeting of October 01, 2012
